name: application-form-row
title: Form Row
description: Label, help text, and error state wired to a real form control with correct id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid associations.
useWhen: Building a form field that needs a label, optional help text, and an error state with correct accessibility wiring.
Wrapping an existing input, select, or textarea component so it gets consistent label and error handling for free.
Replacing hand-rolled label/input/error markup that is re-implemented slightly differently on every form.
avoidWhen: The field has no label — a labelless control usually indicates a missing accessibility requirement, not a case for this component.
You need a full multi-field form layout with grid alignment — compose several form rows inside your own layout instead.
The control is a checkbox or radio group, where the label typically follows rather than precedes the control.
responsiveBehavior: The row is a single-column flex stack at all widths; place it inside your own responsive grid to control multi-column form layouts.
accessibility: The label's htmlFor and the control's id are always associated, whether the control is the built-in input or a child element you pass in.
Help text and error text are linked to the control via aria-describedby so both are announced when the field receives focus.
The control receives aria-invalid when an error is present, and the error text carries role="alert" so screen readers announce it.

variants.title: Form row
variants.description: Label, control, help text, and error state with real id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid wiring, accepting any input as a child.
accessibility: Required fields mark the asterisk aria-hidden and rely on the label text plus form-level instructions to convey the requirement.

variants.title: Form row (Dark)
variants.description: Label, control, help text, and error state adapted for dark form surfaces.
accessibility: Label, help text, and error text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark form backgrounds.
